Total Product & Marginal Product Animator

Drag the worker slider to move simultaneously on both panels. The top panel draws a tangent line on the TP curve

In Fig 5.1 below, slide points along the TP curve to where marginal product peaks and to where it reaches zero; after the
      reveal, slide the point and watch the tangent on TP (whose slope is MPL) and the matching MPL point in the panel under it. This makes the
      "MPL = slope of TP" relationship viscerally clear.

Cobb-Douglas: Q = K0.5 · L0.5. Output is always positive and always increasing in L, but at a decreasing rate. This is the most common textbook production function. MPL falls as L rises (diminishing returns), but never reaches zero.

S-shaped TP: TP = 1.5L2 − 0.1L3, the curve in the film and in Fig 5.1. MPL = 3L − 0.3L2 rises at first, peaks at L = 5 (MPL = 7.5), then falls and reaches zero at L = 10, where TP tops out at 50. A Cobb-Douglas TP such as Q = K0.5 · L0.5 is different: MPL falls from the first worker on (diminishing returns) but never reaches zero.
